joseon.template:
Paint a brand-new, authentic 18th-century Joseon dynasty Korean portrait of the man in this photo, shown as {desc}.

ONE COHERENT HAND-PAINTED IMAGE: the entire picture, including his face, is painted from scratch by a Joseon court painter with fine brush strokes and mineral pigments on aged, slightly yellowed silk, using one muted earthy palette and soft, even light. The face is rendered with the same brushwork, colours and gentle layered shading as the clothes and background. No photographic texture, lighting or sharpness anywhere, nothing that looks pasted in.

LIKENESS: study his face in the photo and paint it so friends would recognise him at once: the same face shape and jawline, the same eye shape and eye size, eyelids, eyebrows, nose, lips, ears, skin tone, age, moles and any facial hair. Do not beautify, slim, age or cartoonify him.

PERIOD LOOK: replace his modern haircut with a period-correct style; no modern bangs or fringe visible. For a man's role, unless the role says otherwise, his hair is gathered into a topknot (sangtu) with a black horsehair headband (manggeon) across the forehead, under the hat that suits the role. For a woman's role (queen, princess, lady, maiden, court lady, tavern keeper, female dancer and so on), this is a playful, humorous portrait: paint HIM, still clearly the same man with his own male face, jaw, skin and any facial hair, wearing that role's women's clothing, hairstyle and accessories with a proud, straight-faced dignity. Do not feminise or beautify his face. Paint round Joseon-era spectacles only if he is clearly wearing glasses in the photo.

POSE: do not copy the photo's pose, hand gestures, head tilt, clothing or background. Use a dignified, natural pose that suits the role, seated or standing, front or three-quarter view, hands relaxed or holding the role's prop, with correctly painted hands and realistic proportions. If the role is a figure from Korean folklore, paint it as a Joseon-era folk painting of that legend while keeping his face.

COMPOSITION: tall vertical hanging-scroll format, framed from about the knees or waist up so his face is clearly visible, simple uncluttered background suited to the role, and an empty area of plain silk in the upper right corner.

Do not write any text, letters, hanja, calligraphy or red seals anywhere. No modern clothing or modern objects.

grandprince.name: 대군
grandprince.desc: a Joseon grand prince (daegun) in a rich purple silk robe with a gold-embroidered roundel on the chest and a black samo hat, seated in an elegant palace study

policechief.name: 포도대장
policechief.desc: the chief of the Joseon police bureau in a red military robe (gunbok) with a black jeonrip hat decorated with a peacock feather, holding a command baton

archer.name: 신궁
archer.desc: a legendary master archer in a dark indigo martial robe with tied sleeves and a black jeonrip hat, drawing a traditional Korean horn bow at an archery range

satto.name: 사또
satto.desc: a county magistrate (satto) in a dark blue official robe and a black samo hat, seated on a raised wooden platform in the courtyard of a local government office

pansori.name: 명창
pansori.desc: a famous pansori singer in a white dopo robe and a black gat hat, holding an open folding fan mid-song, with a seated drummer's barrel drum (buk) beside him

geomancer.name: 지관

hunjang.name: 훈장

gwangdae.name: 광대
gwangdae.desc: a cheerful street performer (gwangdae) in colourful hemp clothes and a small hat, balancing on a tightrope with an open folding fan

blacksmith.name: 대장장이
blacksmith.desc: a village blacksmith in rough hemp clothes and a leather apron with a towel around his head, holding a hammer over an anvil beside a glowing forge

woodcutter.name: 나무꾼
woodcutter.desc: a woodcutter in plain hemp clothes carrying a wooden A-frame (jige) piled with firewood, holding an axe on a misty mountain path

daebi.name: 대비
daebi.desc: a dignified queen dowager in a dark purple ceremonial robe with gold phoenix patterns and an ornate formal hairstyle with gold and jade pins, seated on a royal chair before a muted folding screen

consort.name: 후궁
consort.desc: a royal consort (bin) in a rose-pink dangui jacket with gold-leaf patterns and a deep red chima, an elaborate formal hairstyle with jewelled pins, seated in a palace chamber

gayageum.name: 가야금 명인
gayageum.desc: a gayageum virtuoso in an elegant jade-green jeogori and a deep red chima, playing a twelve-string gayageum resting on her lap

damo.name: 다모
damo.desc: a damo (female police investigator) in a dark navy jacket with a red sash and a black head cloth, holding a short sword in its scabbard, sharp and alert

poet.name: 여류 시인
poet.desc: a woman poet in a pale blue jeogori and an indigo chima, writing hangul poetry with a brush on paper at a low desk by a lotus pond

mudang.name: 만신
mudang.desc: a powerful shaman (mudang) in a bright red and blue ceremonial robe and a tall ceremonial hat, holding a fan and a cluster of brass bells, colourful ritual flags behind

kitchen.name: 수라간 나인
kitchen.desc: a royal kitchen court lady in a pale yellow jeogori and a dark blue chima with a neat braided hairstyle, carefully arranging dishes on a royal dining table

haenyeo.name: 해녀
haenyeo.desc: a Jeju diver (haenyeo) in white cotton diving clothes with a net bag and a round orange float (taewak), standing on a black volcanic rocky shore

marketwoman.name: 장터 아낙
marketwoman.desc: a lively market woman in plain hemp clothes and a head scarf, selling fish from a bamboo basket at a busy village market

waterjar.name: 물동이 처녀
waterjar.desc: a village girl in a faded pink jeogori and a navy chima, carrying a clay water jar on her head beside an old stone well

dokkaebi.name: 도깨비
dokkaebi.desc: a legendary dokkaebi from Korean folklore: a mischievous figure in a rough tiger-skin vest over hemp clothes, with two small horns on the forehead, holding a magic wooden club (dokkaebi bangmangi), faint blue will-o'-the-wisp flames floating around him

jeoseung.name: 저승사자

sansin.name: 산신령

doseungji.name: 도승지
doseungji.desc: the king's chief royal secretary (doseungji) in a deep red official robe with a crane rank badge and a black samo hat, holding a royal decree scroll inside the palace

monk.name: 큰스님

horseman.name: 기마무사

falconer.name: 매사냥꾼

bowmaker.name: 궁장
bowmaker.desc: a master bow maker (gungjang) at a wooden workbench, carefully bending a horn bow, with arrows and tools around him

potter.name: 도공
potter.desc: a master potter in hemp clothes at a wooden potter's wheel, shaping a large white porcelain moon jar

chef.name: 숙수
chef.desc: a royal palace cook (suksu) in a white cooking jacket and head cloth, holding a large ladle beside steaming iron pots

hunter.name: 포수

talchum.name: 탈춤꾼
talchum.desc: a mask dancer in a colourful dance costume with long white sleeves, a carved wooden dance mask pushed up on top of his head so his face is fully visible, mid-dance

ssireum.name: 씨름 장사

gamakkun.name: 가마꾼

muljangsu.name: 물장수

jipsin.name: 짚신장수
jipsin.desc: a straw-sandal maker sitting on a straw mat weaving straw sandals (jipsin), with finished pairs hanging beside him

gumiho.name: 구미호

seonnyeo.name: 선녀
seonnyeo.desc: a heavenly maiden (seonnyeo) from Korean folklore in flowing pastel celestial robes with long floating silk ribbons, descending on soft clouds

yongnyeo.name: 용녀
yongnyeo.desc: the Dragon King's daughter from Korean folklore in shimmering blue-green robes decorated with pearls and wave patterns, a small jade dragon crown, rising from the sea holding a glowing pearl

ongju.name: 옹주

sworddancer.name: 검무 명인

haegeum.name: 해금 악사

femalearcher.name: 여궁사

teamaster.name: 다인
teamaster.desc: a refined tea master in a cream jeogori and a dusty blue chima, pouring tea from a celadon teapot at a low wooden table

weaver.name: 베 짜는 여인

swing.name: 그네 아씨

apothecary.name: 약방 아씨

bangmul.name: 방물장수
bangmul.desc: a travelling trinket peddler (bangmul-jangsu) with an open cloth bundle of hairpins, mirrors and silk ribbons

onggi.name: 옹기장수

chamoe.name: 참외장수
chamoe.desc: a melon seller with a big basket of yellow Korean melons (chamoe) at a summer market

neolttwigi.name: 널뛰기 소녀

mgumiho.name: 구미호

yongwang.name: 용왕

seson.name: 세손

daewongun.name: 대원군

panseo.name: 판서

daejehak.name: 대제학

buma.name: 부마
buma.desc: the king's son-in-law (buma) in an elegant jade-green silk robe and a black samo hat, seated in a palace garden

wangja.name: 왕자
wangja.desc: a Joseon prince in a bright red robe with gold patterns and a black hat with a jade ornament, seated on a carved chair in the palace

hyeopgaek.name: 협객
hyeopgaek.desc: a wandering swordsman (hyeopgaek) in a dark indigo martial robe and a wide black gat hat with a long bead strap, holding a sword in its scabbard on a windy hillside

naegwan.name: 내관
naegwan.desc: a palace eunuch (naegwan) in a dark green robe and a black hat, holding a white horsehair whisk, standing respectfully in a palace corridor

calligrapher.name: 서예가
calligrapher.desc: a master calligrapher in a white robe and a black gat hat, holding a large brush over a sheet of paper at a low desk with an ink stone

geomungo.name: 거문고 명인

baksu.name: 박수무당

baduk.name: 바둑 고수
baduk.desc: a baduk (Go) master in a white robe and a black gat hat, seated before a wooden Go board mid-game, holding a stone between two fingers

daemokjang.name: 대목장

monggi.name: 옹기장수

mchamoe.name: 참외장수
mchamoe.desc: a melon seller with a big basket of yellow Korean melons (chamoe) at a summer market

gambler.name: 투전꾼
